## f99497dd2d28

**AUD-F994-CANONICAL-BRANCH-GAP — Reproduced canonical-domain and teaching defect.**

Audited generator SHA-256 `1682c78d4d5ee835adb862e1bc8a8e97798b23948b4c9a572fd1fed366667385`; executed canonical Racket rule hash `191d0a6cff5a`.

The selected rule has a real third branch condition: an LR-symmetric shape produces a horizontal center line only when it is not UD-symmetric **or** its bounding-box height is odd. An LR+UD-symmetric shape with even height must therefore produce a vertical line.

The current generator never emits that canonical branch. Its `row` branch creates LR-symmetric odd-height shapes; its `col` branch creates non-LR shapes. Its own validator rejects canonical training pair index 3 with:

`LR-symmetric shape should have odd bbox height to trigger the horizontal branch`

That canonical input is LR- and UD-symmetric with bbox height 4. Public Racket execution draws the vertical center column, while the simpler rival “draw a horizontal center row iff the crop is LR-symmetric; otherwise vertical” draws a horizontal row. The exact input, both outputs, validator result and source/rule hashes are in `checks/audit/f99497dd2d28/witness.json`.

The same rival matched public Racket on **30/30 current emitted probes** (10 per band; 15 LR and 15 non-LR), all valid under `self_check`. Thus generated lessons cannot distinguish the rival, while a canonical task input does. The isolated audit preset also failed because no semantic contract or task-local tests are declared (`checks/audit/f99497dd2d28-combined/result.json`).

Suggested repair: add the LR+UD+even-height column branch to ordinary generation and strict canonical support; then declare executable branch witnesses/rivals and add portable task tests. Audit only; source left unchanged.

Evidence: `checks/audit/f99497dd2d28/input.json`, `probe-pre-racket.json`, `racket.json`, `witness.json`, and the combined audit report.
